sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What technique is most commonly used to show a drawing of a car is 'on the move'?
options: A) Drawing the car very small
B) Adding speed lines or blurred wheels
C) Painting it with very dark colors
D) Drawing a thick, heavy border around it
questions.answer: B) Adding speed lines or blurred wheels

questions.question_text: When an artist uses a window frame in their composition (Peeping Out of the Window), what does it act as?
options: A) A natural border that creates perspective
B) A tool to mix paint
C) A way to make the paper heavier
D) A method to hide mistakes
questions.answer: A) A natural border that creates perspective

questions.question_text: In 'Picturing Stories', how do comic artists usually show what a character is saying?
options: A) They write it at the very bottom of the page
B) They use speech bubbles pointing to the mouth
C) They draw the words hiding behind trees
D) They use only hand gestures without any text
questions.answer: B) They use speech bubbles pointing to the mouth

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes creating 'Imaginary Beings' in art?
options: A) Drawing a realistic self-portrait
B) Sketching a normal house
C) Combining parts of different animals to invent a new creature
D) Tracing a photograph of a real cat
questions.answer: C) Combining parts of different animals to invent a new creature

questions.question_text: What is the most important element when making a poster for 'Spreading the Message'?
options: A) Using very tiny, faint text
B) Bold, readable text and eye-catching colors
C) Only using shades of gray
D) Drawing very complicated, confusing patterns
questions.answer: B) Bold, readable text and eye-catching colors

questions.question_text: When you 'Create a Scene', what do we call the objects placed closest to the viewer at the bottom of the picture?
options: A) The background
B) The sky
C) The middle ground
D) The foreground

questions.question_text: Which materials are primarily used for the 'Stitch it for a Story' technique?
options: A) Clay and water
B) Fabric, needle, and colorful threads
C) Wood and carving knives
D) Watercolor and heavy brushes
questions.answer: B) Fabric, needle, and colorful threads

questions.question_text: What is the main benefit of the 'Time Team Technique' in art projects?
options: A) It allows multiple artists to collaborate and finish a large mural quickly
B) It teaches you how to draw clocks perfectly
C) It forces you to paint in complete silence
D) It uses only one single color for the whole artwork
questions.answer: A) It allows multiple artists to collaborate and finish a large mural quickly

questions.question_text: When you 'View and Review' a classmate's artwork, what should you do?
options: A) Ignore it completely
B) Provide constructive feedback on what they did well and what could improve
C) Erase their work
D) Only complain about the colors used
questions.answer: B) Provide constructive feedback on what they did well and what could improve

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT a visual arts technique?
options: A) Applique stitching
B) Poster designing
C) Singing scales in different tempos
D) Storyboarding panels
questions.answer: C) Singing scales in different tempos

questions.question_text: Explain how you would sketch a race car to show it is 'on the move'. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I would add horizontal action lines behind the car, draw heavily blurred wheels, and tilt the car slightly forward to create a strong illusion of fast speed.

questions.question_text: Why is using a 'window frame' helpful when drawing a landscape composition? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: It acts as a natural border, helping the artist focus strictly on a specific part of the scenery and easily creating depth through framed perspective.

questions.question_text: Describe a unique 'Imaginary Being' you could draw for an art project. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An imaginary being could be a creature featuring the strong, muscular body of a lion, the colorful, vibrant wings of a parrot, and a dragon's tail.

questions.question_text: What is the primary goal of creating a poster in the 'Spreading the Message' activity? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The main goal is to catch people's attention instantly using bold colors and clear, large text to communicate an important public message effectively.

questions.question_text: How do artists use 'Picturing Stories' to show what a character is thinking instead of speaking? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Artists use thought bubbles, which look like fluffy clouds with small circles trailing down to the character's head, to clearly show internal thoughts or ideas.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are using the 'Stitch it for a Story' technique to depict a magical night forest. Describe your materials and design. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would use a thick dark blue fabric as the night sky. For the trees, I would stitch patches of brown felt and use bright yellow thread to embroider small glowing fireflies, creating a beautiful, highly textured, and magical night forest scene.

questions.question_text: Describe a poster you would create for 'Spreading the Message' about protecting ocean life. What visuals and colors would you use? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would paint a giant, sad blue whale surrounded by dark, polluted gray water. Above it, I would write 'Keep Our Oceans Clean' in bright, bold yellow letters to quickly grab the viewer's attention and effectively spread this vital environmental message.

questions.question_text: Explain how your class can use the 'Time Team Technique' to paint a massive mural of a busy city street scene. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, we would divide the large canvas into specific sections. One group sketches the background skyscrapers, another paints the busy pedestrians in the foreground, and the last group adds colorful details like traffic lights. Working cooperatively saves time and perfectly combines everyone's unique creative skills into one masterpiece.

questions.question_text: When asked to 'Create a Scene' of a stormy day, explain step-by-step how you would separate the foreground, middle ground, and background. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would start the background with dark gray storm clouds and distant, faded mountains. In the middle ground, I would draw tall trees bending sharply in the strong wind. For the foreground, I would paint bright red umbrellas and detailed rain puddles right at the very front of the picture.
